jobs.occupation: Researcher in Biostatistics
jobs.description:
About the position
We are seeking applicants with a strong methodological background in biostatistics and causal inference for a 3-year 20% researcher position in Biostatistics, in a project on causal inference for effects of health related interventions on working life outcomes, at the Oslo Centre for Biostatistics and Epidemiology (OCBE), Department of Biostatistics, University of Oslo (UiO).
 
OCBE is one of Europe's most active biostatistics groups with currently about 80 researchers. OCBE is internationally recognized, with interests spanning a broad range of areas, including causal inference and time-to-event analysis, clinical trials, epidemiology, high dimensional statistics, infectious disease, machine learning and mathematical modelling. The centre has numerous collaborations with leading biomedical research groups internationally and in Norway.
More about the position
The candidate will be part of the research group on causal inference and survival analysis led by professor Jon Michael Gran, where they will work on causal inference with applications to longitudinal data from large population-wide registries. The position is connected to the project “Improving causal inference for individual working life trajectories from registry data: studying interventions, estimands and heterogeneity”, funded by the Research Council of Norway (RCN). The project is a close collaboration with research groups at the National Institute of Occupational Health (STAMI) and Oslo University Hospital (OUS).

The candidate will pursue research on causal inference for treatment effect estimation from complex longitudinal data, collected from various population wide registries. An emphasis will be made on exposure measurement error, interference, effect heterogeneity and the analysis of individual outcome trajectories. However, other methods may also be relevant. Methods should be motivated in and applied to answering the subject matter research questions of the overall project, such as of the effects of interventions for a more inclusive working life (including rehabilitation measures and work place facilitation) or the effects of sustained medical treatments (including use of opioids and other type of pain treatment for patients after traumatic injury). Outcomes of interest will be related to long term health, sick leave and work participation. 

The candidate’s role in the project will be both to supervise other project members and to conduct own methodological and applied research in biostatistics. We provide an exciting and friendly research environment for the development and application of new methods in a collaborative and interdisciplinary fashion, with various national and international collaborators. The candidate will work closely with other project members at OCBE, STAMI and OUS, other external collaborators, and the causal inference and survival analysis group at OCBE. The candidate will participate in regular project meetings and must have the ability to work well in a multi-disciplinary team.

The candidate’s workplace will be at OCBE’s premises in the UiO building Domus Medica.

Preferred starting date for the position is January 1st, 2027. 
Qualifications requirements
Required quialifications:

• Applicants must hold a degree corresponding to a Norwegian doctoral degree in biostatistics or statistics. 
• A broad background from methodological research in causal inference is required. 
• Strong quantitative and computational skills is required. Applicants should be fluent in R or equivalent software.
• Experience with interdisciplinary collaborations and student supervision at PhD level is required. 
Desired qualifications:

• Experience within areas relevant for the project will be an advantage.
• Experience with analysis of large datasets is an advantage. Experience with biomedical applications is also an advantage.
• Personal suitability will be emphasized.
Language requirements:

• Working language in the group and at OCBE is English. Fluent oral and written communication skills in English is required. Personal skills
• Ability to work independently and efficiently.
• Good communication and collaborative skills.
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications.

For particularly well-qualified applicants, a higher salary may be considered. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund.

Application

jobs.description:
The Departments of Solar Power Systems and Energy System Analysis at the Institute for Energy Technology (IFE) have a vacant PhD research fellowship focused on modelling how increasing photovoltaic (PV) generation affects Norwegian power grids. The position is part of the KSP project Solvar and the Norwegian PV Research Centre (FME SOLAR) and combines regional PV production modelling with power system analysis to support safe and cost-effective integration of solar power. 

The Departments of Solar Power Systems and Energy System Analysis at IFE conduct research on PV systems analysis (including performance and forecasting of PV plants), and energy system modelling (including techno-economic modelling and power flow analysis). The candidate will be supervised by a team of researchers from IFE and the University of Oslo with strong competence in the generation and distribution of electricity. The PhD will be affiliated with the Department of Technology Systems at the University of Oslo.

The PhD candidate will work on robust power grids and regional PV production profiles. The research will develop realistic regional PV models adapted to Norwegian conditions and integrate them into power system models of selected real use cases in the distribution grid. Particular attention will be given to spatial smoothing, simultaneity and ramping of distributed PV, reliable grid integration of PV, as well as the interaction between PV, wind power and run-of-river hydropower. The results will help grid operators assess hosting capacity, operational risks and suitable measures for integrating more PV. The work will combine physical grid and PV modelling, data analysis and selected data-driven methods. Regional PV profiles may be investigated for spatial scales ranging from individual transformers and feeders to larger regions. Validation will use measured and historical PV data, irradiance data, building information and grid data made available through the project and open data sources.   In addition to being integrated into internationally leading research groups at IFE, the candidate will have the opportunity to collaborate with other world-class research communities, e.g., through the International Energy Agency’s Photovoltaic Power Systems Programme Task 16 & 19, and through contributions to the Pan-European Climate Database. The candidate should have strong competence in energy systems, have experience with PV or power systems modelling from before and be highly proficient in spoken and written English. It is also an advantage if the candidate has experience of working with Norwegian PV or grids and is proficient in a Scandinavian language.  We seek a candidate with a positive attitude and good communication skills, who can work independently, but also participate actively in the research group. The position will be in a expanding research field with many actors, requiring an ambitious candidate with strong collaborative qualities. The candidate will work in an active and growing research field at IFE, in a young and social work environment. jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We invite applications for a 3-year PhD Candidate position on the future role of hydrogen and hydrogen products in industrial decarbonization. The position is based at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management, located at NTNU’s campus in Trondheim.

The mission of Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management (IØT) is to carry out education, research, and innovation activities at an international level at the intersection between technology/natural sciences and business economics, management, and HSE. The department’s activities aim to contribute to sustainable value creation within technology-based areas in industry, business, and the public sector in Norway

 

About the position

Electrification is widely promoted as a key pathway to industrial decarbonization. At the same time, hydrogen and carbon capture and storage (CCS) are increasingly recognized as important solutions for sectors where direct electrification may be difficult or uneconomic. This has led to a growing debate about the future role of "electrons versus molecules" in a net-zero economy.

Most existing studies assume that today's industrial structure remains largely unchanged and focus on how current industries can reduce emissions. However, deep decarbonization may fundamentally reshape industrial production, value chains, competitiveness, and the location of energy-intensive activities. As a result, future hydrogen demand may depend as much on industrial transformation as on technological choices.

This PhD project will investigate how alternative pathways toward a zero-emission industrial sector affect the future demand for hydrogen and the development of hydrogen value chains. The research will analyze the interplay between electrification, hydrogen, and CCS, while explicitly accounting for potential changes in industrial structures and production systems.

 

The project addresses research questions like:

• How will future hydrogen demand vary across alternative industrial decarbonization pathways?
• Which industrial sectors are likely to rely on electrification, hydrogen, or CCS to achieve net-zero emissions?
• How might industrial transformation affect hydrogen production, transport, storage, and trade?
• What level of hydrogen deployment is required to justify dedicated hydrogen infrastructure and markets?
• How can Europe and Norway prepare for different industrial and energy-system transition pathways?
 

The successful candidate will develop and analyze future scenarios for industrial transformation, hydrogen demand, and infrastructure development. The project will contribute to the scientific and policy debate on how competitive zero-emission industries can emerge under different transition strategies.
Research environment
The PhD candidate will join a multidisciplinary research environment at the intersection of energy economics, industrial economics, operations research, and energy systems analysis.

The position is affiliated with FME HYDROGENi, the Norwegian Research and Innovation Centre for Hydrogen and Ammonia. The centre brings together 46 research and industry partners to develop the knowledge, technologies, and solutions needed to support a sustainable hydrogen economy and contribute to Norway's ambitions for climate neutrality and industrial transformation. FME HYDROGENi conducts research across the hydrogen value chain, including hydrogen production, transport and storage, industrial and maritime applications, safety, and the broader role of hydrogen in future energy systems. The centre is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Centres for Environment-friendly Energy Research (FME) programme and operates during the period 2022-2030

The PhD candidate will be hosted at the Managerial Economics, Finance and Operations Research (BEDØK) group at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management. The group is one of Norway’s leading academic environments in operations research, logistics, optimization, and quantitative decision support. The candidate will work in close collaboration with researchers from NTNU’s Department of Computer Science and Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Your role in the project
The PhD candidate will:

• Conduct original scientific research on hydrogen and industrial decarbonization pathways.
• Develop and analyze scenarios for industrial transformation and climate neutrality.
• Assess the future role of electrification, hydrogen, and CCS across industrial sectors.
• Quantify hydrogen demand and infrastructure requirements under alternative transition pathways.
• Publish research results in leading international journals and conferences.
• Collaborate with academic, industry, and public-sector partners.
• Complete the required coursework as part of the PhD programme.
• Contribute to dissemination and communication of research findings.
 

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Qualification requirements
Applicants must hold a master’s degree in a relevant field with strong academic results (B or better according to NTNU’s grading scale). Relevant academic backgrounds include:

• Operations research or optimization
• Energy systems
• Energy Economics
• Engineering disciplines with strong quantitative and analytical content
• Or other closely related disciplines.
Applicants must demonstrate strong analytical and quantitative skills.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Desired qualifications
The following qualifications will be considered an advantage:

• Experience with energy system modelling, scenario analysis, or techno-economic analysis.

• Experience with quantitative modelling and data analysis.

Applicants in the final phase of their master’s studies are encouraged to apply.
Personal characteristics
We are looking for a candidate who:

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

Video: https://youtu.be/Xt-yHCN5QS0About the position
For a position as a PhD Candidate, the goal is a completed doctoral education up to an obtained doctoral degree.

We are looking for a PhD candidate for one of 13 PhD positions in Marie Sklodowska-Curie Action (MSCA) CHARM (Conservation of Heritage Architecture, buildings and sites by Resilient Methods: hydro-climate factors) project. The main objective of CHARM MSCA Doctoral Network project is to develop new sustainable conservation and restoration solutions, adapted to the current and future climate conditions, designed in a circular economy philosophy, having a low environmental footprint and high handprint. CHARM also responds to socio-economical requirements of wellbeing and proposes conservation/restoration solutions economically acceptable and respecting the cultural value of buildings.

CHARM proposes a holistic approach including:

• Site observation and data collection
• Data preparation to be used by AI, models, etc
• Methods for understanding and modelling past and future degradation of architectural heritage
• Sustainable conservation solutions to several observed problems
• Assessment of the impact of architectural conservation on the environment and of the environment (past, present and future) on architectural heritage
• Bidirectional interactions with society proposing risk management plans but also taking into account the society wills and needs
The vision of CHARM MSCA project is to educate young and talented scientists towards a combined high-level experimental and data driven approach for the early-stage accurate, precise detection of hydro-climate impact on cultural heritage, to answer to recruitment needs in time of climate change and natural hazards impact about research and innovation in the sector of cultural heritage conservation and restoration. 

CHARM network gathers excellent academic centers that have decennial experience in the field of risk assessment, adaptation and mitigation solutions to the climate change impact, conservation of cultural heritage and restoration, documented by scientific papers published in high impact-factor journals, and by previous EU funded research projects. CHARM puts together researchers from universities and research organisms, national and local organizations in charge of Cultural Heritage conservation, Small and Midsize Enterprises, industrial producer of building materials, and Non-Governmental Organization, from 9 European and 1 South American countries.
Description of DC2 PhD position
Project title: Understanding conservation condition and rehabilitation needs at district scale in time of energy saving and climate change via machine learning driven method

Topic in brief:

The aim is to implement an approach based on artificial intelligence (AI) in the form of CNN to automatically detect cracks and morphological indices in order to manage the large amount of data obtained from photogrammetry and earth observations images.

Objectives:

This doctoral project aims to develop deep learning neural networks to investigate data in available database (e.g., EU building stock observatory and other similar database) to:

• classify building stock at district scale more prone to decay based on buildings construction year, location, main constitutive material, exposure, use and
• to predict potential maintenance and restoration priority based on (i) and existing energy retrofit directive and/or risk maps 
Expected results:

(i)to build high-quality dataset highlighting the façade that is more prone to decay at district/city level from existing raw database; 

(ii) to apply deep learning neural networks (e.g., convolutional neural network) to perform semi-automatic decay pattern segmentation and associated mapping; 

(iii) to correlate the maintenance of buildings at district/city level with decay patterns/features at district scale to prioritize large scale intervention; and 

(iv) to optimize the maintenance activities by leveraging these correlations learned by machine-learning based approaches. 

Supervisory Committee:

• Main supervisor: Full prof. Chiara Bertolin, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) (Academic)
• Co-supervisor: Associate prof. Chao Gao, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) (Academic)
• Mentor: Dr. Marie Louise Anker, Department Director at Nidaros Cathedral Restoration Works. (Non.Academic)
 

Planned secondments

SECONDMENT 1 - Prof. P. Fafalios (FORTH Foundation for Research and Technology – Hellas, Crete) M12, duration: 4 weeks, AI and ML algorithms,

SECONDMENT 2 - Prof. Carradò (CY Cergy Paris University) Karima El Ganaoui, ESTI Pau CY Tech, M24, duration: 4 weeks, AI materials
Duties of the position
• Take part in the mandatory PhD research education programme
• Develop a quantitative deep-learning-based framework to detect the micro-cracks and validate the developed framework
• Define micro-scale indices to evaluate crack morphological characteristics and validate developed the indices
• Classify the micro-morphologies and damages of undamage and damage materials and/or hazard prone or not buildings and landscape
• Participate in other relevant research and dissemination activities through our international collaborators
• Conduct and publish high-level research at peer-reviewed journals and international conferences
• Carry on condition monitoring campaigns and surveys in situ
• Write and defend a PhD thesis
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Statistics, Materials Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering or equivalent. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you maybe considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme
• Excellent written and oral English
• Strong background in applying deep learning neural networks on image segmentation associated with materials and the built environment
• Excellent programming skills in Python and Matlab
PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria

If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Ved Universitetet i Agder, Fakultet for helse- og idrettsvitenskap er det ledig en 100% stilling som postdoktor i idrettsvitenskap, tilknyttet Institutt for idrettsvitenskap og kroppsøving, for en periode på tre, eventuelt fire år. Arbeidssted er for tiden Campus Kristiansand. Tiltredelse etter avtale med fakultetet.

Fakultetet har fem institutter: Institutt for ernæring og folkehelse, Institutt for helse- og sykepleievitenskap, Institutt for idrettsvitenskap og kroppsøving, Institutt for psykologi og Institutt for psykososial helse. Postdoktorstillingen vil være tilknyttet forskningsgruppen PAHLS (Physical Activity and Health across the LifeSpan). I tillegg har instituttet forskningsgruppene SPADE (Sport Performance and Development Environments) og ROPE (Research in Outdoor Education and Physical Education).
Arbeidsoppgaver
I samarbeid med nasjonale og internasjonale forskningsinstitusjoner, kreftforeningen, rehabiliteringsinstitusjon og flere kommuner på Agder, og basert på erfaringer gjort i LETSGO-forskningsprosjekt (Lifestyle and Empowerment Techniques in Survivorship of Gynecologic Oncology - Universitetet i Agder), skal det utvikles en digital smarttelefonapplikasjon (app) med tilhørende opplæringsmodul. Denne skal utvikles sammen med brukere (individer berørt av kreft, helsearbeidere) og inneholde ulike fysisk aktivitets- og treningskomponenter. Videre skal denne implementeres i flere frisklivssentraler i kommuner på Agder. Vi skal evaluere implementeringen av denne. Deretter skal det lages en plan for hvordan app og opplæringsmodul kan rulles ut til alle landets kommuner. 

Den som ansettes vil sammen med prosjektleder ha ansvar for å utvikle studieprotokoll, kvalitetssikring av datainnsamling, harmonisering av data og koordinering av prosjektsamarbeidet mellom de involverte aktører involvert i prosjekter. Vedkommende skal også ha et spesielt ansvar for utviklingen av applikasjonen (sammen med andre forskere ved UiA samt UiAs IT-avdeling) samt implementeringsdelen i prosjektet. I tillegg skal det skrives forskningsartikler på allerede innsamlede og kommende data innenfor fagfeltet fysisk aktivitet/trening ved kreftsykdom. Det forventes at den aktuelle postdoktoren skal drive selvstendig forskning innen rammene for det nevnte prosjektet. Dersom det er aktuelt med undervisning/veiledning legges det også til rette for at kandidaten kan følge kurs i universitetspedagogikk (UniPed). Det er også ønskelig at kandidaten følger karriereutviklingsprogram alla postdoktorprogram. Den som tilsettes i stillingen vil få én faglig veileder.
Nødvendige kvalifikasjoner
Doktorgrad i idrettsvitenskap eller fagområde med relevans for utlysningen. Aktuelle søkere må ha fått godkjent avhandlingen innen søknadsfristen

Arbeidsspråket ved Universitetet i Agder er norsk. Den som ansettes må beherske norsk eller et annet skandinavisk språk, skriftlig og muntlig. Det kreves gode kunnskaper i engelsk, skriftlig og muntlig. 

Ansettelsesvilkår for stilling som postdoktor fremgår av Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven.
Ønskede kvalifikasjoner
• Erfaring fra prosjektledelse eller koordinering av prosjekter
• Erfaring med bruk av bevegelsesmålere-/sensorer (aktivitetsmålere, pulsklokker m.m.) i prosjekter
• God teknologisk innsikt; blant annet bruk av smarttelefonapplikasjoner i forskning
• Erfaring med forskning innenfor fagfeltet trening/fysisk aktivitet ved kreftsykdom
• Kjennskap til implementeringsdesign og -metoder
• Erfaring med kvantitative forskningsmetoder, spesialt longitudinelle design
• Det er ønskelig at søkerne har disputert i løpet av de siste fem årPersonlige egenskaper
• Selvstendig
• Gode samarbeidsegenskaper
• Faglig engasjement
• Evne til å sette seg inn i nye problemstillinger og metodetilnærminger
Personlige egenskaper og egnethet for stillingen vil bli vektlagt.
Vi tilbyr
• Faglig utvikling i en stor, spennende og samfunnsviktig organisasjon
• Et godt, inkluderende og mangfoldig arbeidsmiljø
• Moderne lokaliteter og et allsidig velferdstilbud
• Medlemskap i Statens pensjonskasse
Mer om UiA som arbeidsplass.

Stillingen lønnes etter Statens lønnsregulativ lønnsplan 17.510, kode 1352 postdoktor, kr. 690 000 – 750 000 brutto pr år. For spesielt godt kvalifiserte søkere kan høyere lønn vurderes. Fra lønnen går det lovfestet innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse. 
Generell informasjon
UiA er et åpent og inkluderende universitet. Vi har tro på at mangfold beriker arbeidsplassen og gjør oss bedre. Vi oppfordrer derfor kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke uavhengig av kjønn, alder, kulturell bakgrunn, nedsatt funksjonsevne eller “hull i CV-en". 

Kvinner oppfordres spesielt til å søke stillingen. 

Den som ansettes, har rettigheter og plikter etter de retningslinjer som til enhver tid gjelder for stillingen. Ansettelse foretas av Ansettelsesutvalget for undervisnings- og forskerstillinger ved Universitetet i Agder.

jobs.occupation: Site Supervisor – Data Centre Projects
jobs.description:
Lead the work where it happens.
Fortica builds and finishes data centres across Norway and the Nordics. As Site Supervisor you lead the daily work on site and make sure it is done safely, on time and to the right quality.
What you will do
• 
Supervise and coordinate daily work on site: our own crews and subcontractors

• 
Make sure the work follows the drawings, the plan and the quality requirements

• 
Do site inspections and find quality, safety or schedule problems early

• 
Follow the safety rules together with the Site Manager and HSE Advisor

• 
Keep site records and progress reports up to date

• 
Take part in coordination meetings with the client and other contractors

Our scope on site: ceilings, sandwich panels (insulated wall and roof panels), flashing, penetration sealing, finishing works and site services.
Who you are
• 
2+ years' experience as a supervisor or foreman in construction

• 
Experience from data centres, industrial or commercial buildings is a plus

• 
You can read construction drawings and follow specifications

• 
You know safety and quality on a construction site

• 
Good English, spoken and written

• 
Driving licence class B

• 
Flexible and mobile: willing to travel and work on projects in Norway and abroad
What makes you a good fit
You are hands-on and organised. You give clear instructions, follow up your team and speak up when something is not right. Safety and quality always come first for you.
What we offer
• 
3:1 rotation (3 weeks on, 1 week off) with flights, accommodation and meals covered

• 
4 % pension and health insurance

• 
We help you get your HMS card (the Norwegian ID card for everyone working on a construction site) if you do not have one

• 
Real responsibility on large, modern projects

• 
A safe workplace with fair terms and a written employment contract

• 
Part of CTS Group, one of Europe's leading data centre design and build groups

You report to: Site ManagerLocations: Narvik, Kristiansand and Fyresdal, Norway
